blocked_passes: near_ideal
acceptable
No network-adequacy pass: HSD/ACC pass or exception approval does not prove active provider availability or appointment access.
No provider-directory pass: MPF/API directory presence does not prove the provider is active, accepts the enrollee, or has timely appointments.
No behavioral-health workforce pass: nominal provider supply does not prove active Medicare/MA managed-care access.
No encounter-data payment-denial pass: adjustment codes without a definitive denied-claim indicator cannot certify payment-denial or restoration incidence.
No rebate-value pass: supplemental-benefit or rebate availability does not prove beneficiary use, adequate value, or offsetting claim-security harm.
No risk-score pass: a paid risk-adjusted capitation amount does not prove diagnoses were clinically supported or linked to care.
No HRA/chart-review pass: diagnoses from HRAs or chart reviews without service-record linkage cannot certify payment accuracy or care follow-up.
No RADV-existence pass: a RADV audit route, audited-contract list, or final rule does not prove recovery for the contract/service row under review.
No rate-announcement pass: CMS aggregate payment updates do not prove contract-level claim security, taxpayer neutrality, or beneficiary remedy.
No quality-bonus pass: Star/QBP/rebate context cannot substitute for actual denied-care correctness, access availability, and restoration.
No encounter-data pass: MA encounter records can show furnished-service traces but cannot by themselves prove denied services, payment, cost-sharing, or restoration.
No PBP/offered-benefit pass: approved plan benefits and PBP offerings do not prove eligibility, use, denial, payment, or remedy.
No supplemental-benefit-utilization pass: furnished/approved benefit use and costs cannot reveal denied supplemental benefits unless joined to request/denial records.
No enrollment-neutral pass: a denial/remedy row cannot certify claim security if the beneficiary entered the plan through unbound broker, TPMO, lead-generator, or HCP referral incentives.
No broker-disclosure pass: commission existence, disclosure, or compensation caps do not prove unbiased plan selection or a complete plan universe.
No complaint-only pass: a marketing complaint, CTM entry, or correction right does not prove beneficiary restoration or suitable coverage.
No Medigap-exit pass: switching rights cannot be assumed without guaranteed-issue status, underwriting barrier, premium feasibility, and serious-illness context.
No DOJ-allegation pass: enforcement allegations are contradiction-risk evidence until adjudicated or independently verified.

public_balance_sheet_register.maximum_exposure: OASDI/HI/SMI obligations plus MA payment-integrity exposure, beneficiary premiums/general revenue, provider/payment stress, and prior-authorization denial/delay costs. Exact MA exposure requires contract-level coding/risk-score, bid/rebate, margin, audit/recovery, quality, network, and prior-authorization records. Rev0372 reframes exact exposure as a contract-level join among Part C reporting, validated LDS, monthly enrollment denominators, RADV audited-contract results, and UM internal coverage criteria.
public_balance_sheet_register.expected_loss: Not a single default-loss estimate; risk appears as scheduled-benefit haircuts, premium/tax increases, provider-payment pressure, access constraints, or general-revenue crowdout.
public_balance_sheet_register.stress_scenario: OASI/OASDI depletion or Medicare financing stress arrives before durable repair, so claimants, providers, workers, and future budgets absorb unresolved incidence through automatic cuts, tax increases, premium shifts, access reductions, or debt-financed repair.
public_balance_sheet_register.funding_source: Payroll taxes, trust-fund reserves, beneficiary premiums, general revenue, provider-payment policy, debt issuance, and future repair legislation.
public_balance_sheet_register.loss_sharing: Repair must assign risk to taxpayers/premium payers, plans, providers, coding/utilization-management contractors, and beneficiaries explicitly; public support or payment drift requires audit recoupment, rate adjustment, penalties, disclosure, and beneficiary remedies before ordinary claimants absorb delay or haircut.
public_balance_sheet_register.public_upside_recovery: Public recovery can include MA risk-adjustment correction, RADV/audit recoupment, bid/rebate recalibration, denial penalties, automatic care approval or expedited appeals, data disclosure, beneficiary compensation, and contractor/parent-entity accountability. Certification now specifically requires RADV result/recovery amounts, rate/bid/rebate corrections, disclosure of criteria/outcome mismatches, and beneficiary remedies at contract or plan-service level.
public_balance_sheet_register.ordinary_claimant_protection: Protect low-income retirees, disabled workers, survivors, dual eligibles, high-care-need beneficiaries, and caregivers before protecting tax expenditures, asset subsidies, or provider/intermediary rents.
public_balance_sheet_register.sunset_or_review: Quarterly while 2026 trustees-report assumptions and repair proposals are being digested; annual trustees refresh thereafter.
